newsitem.title: ROMANIA: RADIO ROMANIA AFTERNOON HEADLINES AT 1 PM.
newsitem.headline: RADIO ROMANIA AFTERNOON HEADLINES AT 1 PM.

text.p: * The transport ministry said car owners would have to pay only 42 percent of a new road tax this year, or the equivalent of this annual tax for August-December 1997.
The ministry said public institutions and urban and rural transportation companies were exempt from the tax.
Police are entitled to issue fines if a car owner cannot prove he has paid the tax.
* The government is holding its weekly meeting to debate a social and economic programme for the development of communities in the country's mining regions.
The cabinet is also due to draw measures for the application of a decree to cut down inter-company arrears and debts to the state budget.
* Romanian Defence Minister Victor Babiuc and his Moldovan counterpart Valeriu Pasat met in Bucharest on Thursday to discuss boosting military cooperation.
They signed a bilateral treaty on military transportand agreed to hold joint military drills.
The two ministers will hold a news conference on Friday.
* Education ministry State Secretary Florin Diaconescu has tendered his resignation to Prime Minister Victor Ciorbea in protest against poor management of education reforms.
* Vasile Bostan, head of the private Columna Bank, has resigned, saying he wanted to end the bank's conflicts with the central bank (BNR). Bostan said he also had personal reasons.
The BNR has repeatedly asked for Bostan's removal, saying bank managers are legally required to have at least three years of experience in the field.
Columna's new head is Ortansa Niculescu Petrescu, the bank's vice-president from 1994-1997.
